A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same theoretical bandit study despite the title change. All 14 pages, including the algorithms, equations and Appendix A.1, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 presents algorithms, analytical regret bounds and proofs, including the appendix proof of Lemma 2. It reports no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis results.

after.justification: v3 retains the theoretical study and appendix proof without adding experiments, simulations, user studies or data-analysis outcomes.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 retain identical pseudocode, loss estimators, regularizers, learning rates and distribution updates. The edits to Remark 1 do not change either procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets for training or evaluation. The theoretical setting remains adversarial bandits with unknown switching parameter S; the stochastic-bandit applicability statement is also retained.

E2.justification: The same theoretical regret-bound comparisons with EXP3.S and Bandit-over-Bandit remain in Sections 3.1–3.2. Neither version reports empirical baseline evaluations.

E3.justification: Neither PDF reports an empirical evaluation protocol. No experimental splits, budgets, model configurations or testing procedures are introduced or revised.

E4.justification: Neither version includes ablations, sensitivity experiments, robustness tests or empirical case studies. The theoretical analysis of loss-estimator variance is unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental runs, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Expectations and variance terms in the regret analysis remain unchanged theoretical quantities.

E6.justification: The regret bounds and comparative findings in Sections 3.1–3.2 are unchanged, including the conditions for improving on earlier bounds. Neither version contains empirical result entries.

T1.justification: The regret definition, assumptions, regularizers, Theorems 1–2, Lemmas 1–3 and derivations are retained. Appendix A.1 is identical; the added action-domain qualifier in Remark 1 does not alter its mathematics.

C1.justification: Both versions claim two master-base OMD algorithms for unknown-S switching regret with the same guarantees. Renaming the paper to refer to switching targets does not change the contribution's scope.

C2.justification: The variance-control explanation, interpretation of comparative regret bounds, stochastic-bandit applicability in Remark 2 and open problem of optimal worst-case regret in the conclusion are unchanged.

D1.justification: Parameter prescriptions and implementation formulas are retained. Remark 1's added 'for all a in [d]' makes the existing action domain explicit; no new implementation settings or code/data access information are supplied.

R1.justification: Remark 1 newly attributes the negative-entropy update to Lattimore and Szepesvári (2020) and the log-barrier update to Luo et al. (2022). Both works were already referenced; the bibliography and broader research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Adversarial Bandits Robust to S-Switch Regret' to 'Adversarial Bandits Robust to Switching Targets.' Limited grammar, punctuation, citation-format and author-email edits accompany the singularized 'Problem statement' heading; section organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Edited wording and citations cause small local changes in line wrapping and equation placement. The single-column layout, algorithm displays and appendix placement are retained, with no figures or tables added or removed.

improvement.justification: Light copyediting improves readability, while the explicit source attributions in Remark 1 improve traceability of the update formulas. These are limited editorial benefits: the algorithms, theoretical guarantees and appendix proof remain unchanged.
